_meta.title: Aqeedah
_meta.description: The core beliefs of Islam: the six pillars of Iman and Tawhid.

aqeedah-easy-1.question: How many pillars of Iman (faith) are there in Islam?
aqeedah-easy-1.explanation: The six pillars of Iman are belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree (Qadr).

aqeedah-easy-2.question: What is the Arabic term for the Islamic creed or core beliefs?
aqeedah-easy-2.explanation: Aqeedah refers to the firm, unwavering beliefs that a Muslim holds in the heart regarding matters of faith.

aqeedah-easy-3.question: What is the first pillar of Iman?
aqeedah-easy-3.explanation: Belief in Allah is the foundation of all other pillars of faith and includes affirming His Oneness (Tawhid).

aqeedah-easy-4.question: What does Tawhid mean?
aqeedah-easy-4.explanation: Tawhid is the belief that Allah is One, unique, without partners, and alone deserves all worship.

aqeedah-easy-5.question: Which Surah is often called the Surah of Tawhid?
aqeedah-easy-5.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas purely declares the Oneness of Allah: He is One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is born.

aqeedah-easy-6.question: What is the opposite of Tawhid?
aqeedah-easy-6.explanation: Shirk means associating partners with Allah in His Lordship, worship, or Names and Attributes.

aqeedah-easy-7.question: From what were the angels created?
aqeedah-easy-7.explanation: Angels were created from light, while jinn were created from fire and humans from clay.

aqeedah-easy-8.question: Which angel brought revelation (Wahy) to the Prophets?
aqeedah-easy-8.explanation: Angel Jibril (Gabriel) was tasked with delivering Allah's revelation to the Prophets, including the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

aqeedah-easy-9.question: Which angel will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment?
aqeedah-easy-9.explanation: Israfil is the angel who will blow the Trumpet to signal the end of the world and the resurrection.

aqeedah-easy-10.question: How many primary revealed books are commonly mentioned in Islamic belief?
aqeedah-easy-10.explanation: The four primary books are the Tawrah (Torah), Zabur (Psalms), Injeel (Gospel), and the Quran.

aqeedah-easy-11.question: To which Prophet was the Tawrah revealed?
aqeedah-easy-11.explanation: The Tawrah was revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him.

aqeedah-easy-12.question: To which Prophet was the Zabur revealed?
aqeedah-easy-12.explanation: The Zabur (Psalms) was revealed to Prophet Dawud (David), peace be upon him.

aqeedah-easy-13.question: To which Prophet was the Injeel revealed?
aqeedah-easy-13.explanation: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him.

aqeedah-easy-14.question: Which book is the final revelation from Allah?
aqeedah-easy-14.explanation: The Quran is the final, complete, and preserved revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for all humanity.

aqeedah-easy-15.question: Who is the last and final Messenger of Allah?
aqeedah-easy-15.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets; no prophet will come after him.

aqeedah-easy-16.question: How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?
aqeedah-easy-16.explanation: The Quran mentions 25 Prophets by name, though the total number of Prophets is much greater.

aqeedah-easy-17.question: What is the Arabic term for the Day of Judgment?
aqeedah-easy-17.explanation: Yawm al-Qiyamah refers to the Day of Resurrection when all people will be held accountable for their deeds.

aqeedah-easy-18.question: What does belief in Qadr mean?
aqeedah-easy-18.explanation: Qadr is the belief that everything, good and bad, happens by the knowledge, will, and decree of Allah.

aqeedah-easy-19.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of Iman?
options: Belief in the Five Pillars of Islam
aqeedah-easy-19.explanation: The five pillars of Islam are acts of worship, while the six pillars of Iman are the core beliefs of the heart.

aqeedah-easy-20.question: Who records the deeds of human beings?
aqeedah-easy-20.explanation: The Kiraman Katibin are the noble recording angels who write down every person's good and bad deeds.

aqeedah-easy-21.question: What is the name of the angel who takes the souls at death?
aqeedah-easy-21.explanation: The Angel of Death (often referred to as Izra'il) is responsible for taking the souls of the living when their time ends.

aqeedah-easy-22.question: What is the main message that all Prophets brought?
aqeedah-easy-22.explanation: Every Prophet called their people to Tawhid — the exclusive worship of Allah alone without partners.

aqeedah-easy-23.question: What is the Shahadah?
aqeedah-easy-23.explanation: The Shahadah is the testimony that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger.

aqeedah-easy-24.question: Which of the following is a Name of Allah meaning 'The Most Merciful'?
aqeedah-easy-24.explanation: Ar-Rahman means the Most Merciful, encompassing all of creation with Allah's mercy.

aqeedah-easy-25.question: Do angels have free will like humans?
options: Yes, they can choose to disobey
aqeedah-easy-25.explanation: Angels are obedient servants of Allah who do not disobey His commands and carry them out perfectly.

aqeedah-easy-26.question: What is the belief that Allah has no beginning and no end called in relation to His nature?
aqeedah-easy-26.explanation: Allah is Al-Awwal (the First) and Al-Akhir (the Last); He has no beginning and no end.

aqeedah-easy-27.question: Which Prophet is known as the father of the Prophets (Abul Anbiya)?
aqeedah-easy-27.explanation: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) is called Abul Anbiya because many Prophets came from his lineage.

aqeedah-easy-28.question: What happens on the Day of Judgment according to Islamic belief?
options: People are held accountable for their deeds
aqeedah-easy-28.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, every person will be resurrected and judged based on their beliefs and actions.

aqeedah-easy-29.question: What is Paradise called in Arabic?
aqeedah-easy-29.explanation: Jannah is the eternal abode of reward prepared for the believers who obeyed Allah.

aqeedah-easy-30.question: What is Hellfire called in Arabic?
aqeedah-easy-30.explanation: Jahannam is the abode of punishment prepared for those who rejected faith and committed major sins without repentance.

aqeedah-easy-31.question: Who is the first Prophet in Islam?
aqeedah-easy-31.explanation: Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human and the first Prophet created by Allah.

aqeedah-easy-32.question: What must a Muslim believe about all the Prophets?
options: All Prophets were truthful and sent by Allah
Some Prophets made mistakes in their message
aqeedah-easy-32.explanation: Muslims believe in all Prophets without distinction; all of them conveyed the message of Tawhid truthfully.

aqeedah-easy-33.question: What is the term for the unseen world that includes angels, jinn, and the Hereafter?
aqeedah-easy-33.explanation: Al-Ghayb refers to the unseen realities that cannot be perceived by ordinary human senses but are affirmed by revelation.

aqeedah-easy-34.question: Which of the following is a correct statement about Allah?
options: Allah is One and has no partners
aqeedah-easy-34.explanation: Allah is uniquely One (Ahad). He has no partners, no children, and nothing is comparable to Him.

aqeedah-easy-35.question: What is the reward for those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds?
aqeedah-easy-35.explanation: Allah promises eternal Gardens (Jannah) beneath which rivers flow for those who believe and do good deeds.

aqeedah-easy-36.question: In the Hadith of Jibril, who asked the Prophet ﷺ about Iman?
options: Angel Jibril in the form of a man
aqeedah-easy-36.explanation: Angel Jibril came in the form of a man and asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, Iman, and Ihsan in the famous Hadith of Jibril.

aqeedah-intermediate-1.question: Tawhid is commonly divided by scholars into how many main categories?
aqeedah-intermediate-1.explanation: The three categories are Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah (Lordship), Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Worship), and Tawhid al-Asma wa as-Sifat (Names and Attributes).

aqeedah-intermediate-2.question: What does Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah affirm?
options: Allah is the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Controller
Allah's Names must be affirmed without distortion
aqeedah-intermediate-2.explanation: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah is the belief that Allah alone is the Lord who creates, provides, gives life and death, and manages the universe.

aqeedah-intermediate-3.question: What does Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (or Tawhid al-Ibadah) require?
options: Directing all acts of worship to Allah alone
aqeedah-intermediate-3.explanation: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah means worshipping Allah exclusively — prayer, dua, sacrifice, trust, and love are for Him alone.

aqeedah-intermediate-4.question: What is the correct approach of Ahlus-Sunnah regarding Allah's Names and Attributes?
options: Affirm them as they came without likening to creation or distorting
aqeedah-intermediate-4.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm Allah's Names and Attributes as stated in the Quran and Sunnah, without tashbih (likening), ta'til (denial), or tahrif (distortion).

aqeedah-intermediate-5.question: What is major shirk (shirk akbar)?
options: Associating partners with Allah in a way that takes one out of Islam
aqeedah-intermediate-5.explanation: Major shirk includes worshipping others besides Allah, making dua to the dead, or believing someone shares in Allah's unique rights.

aqeedah-intermediate-6.question: What is minor shirk (shirk asghar)?
options: Actions that diminish pure Tawhid but do not expel from Islam, such as showing off (riya)
aqeedah-intermediate-6.explanation: Minor shirk includes riya (showing off), swearing by other than Allah, and similar acts that compromise sincerity without constituting apostasy.

aqeedah-intermediate-7.question: Which angel is associated with provision and rain?
aqeedah-intermediate-7.explanation: Angel Mika'il is responsible for matters of provision (rizq), including rain and plant growth by Allah's permission.

aqeedah-intermediate-8.question: Who is the guardian of Hellfire?
aqeedah-intermediate-8.explanation: Malik is the chief angel over Hellfire (Jahannam), as mentioned in the Quran.

aqeedah-intermediate-9.question: Who is the guardian of Paradise?
aqeedah-intermediate-9.explanation: Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of the gates of Paradise (Jannah).

aqeedah-intermediate-10.question: What is the difference between a Nabi and a Rasul according to many scholars?
options: A Rasul is sent with a new law or message; every Rasul is a Nabi but not every Nabi is a Rasul
A Nabi is higher in rank
Only Muhammad ﷺ was a Rasul
aqeedah-intermediate-10.explanation: A Nabi (Prophet) receives revelation; a Rasul (Messenger) is additionally sent with a specific message or law to a people.

aqeedah-intermediate-11.question: Who are the five Prophets of strong resolve (Ulul Azm)?
options: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ
aqeedah-intermediate-11.explanation: The Ulul Azm are the five greatest Messengers known for their exceptional patience and resolve in conveying the message.

aqeedah-intermediate-12.question: What must a Muslim believe regarding the previous scriptures?
options: They remain completely unchanged and should be followed today
They were originally from Allah but have been altered; the Quran is the final authority
Only the Injeel is still valid
aqeedah-intermediate-12.explanation: Muslims believe the original Tawrah, Zabur, and Injeel were revelations from Allah, but they underwent change; the Quran abrogates and is protected.

aqeedah-intermediate-13.question: What is the belief about the Quran's nature according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: The Quran is the uncreated Speech of Allah
The Quran is only the meaning, not the words
The Quran is a human composition
aqeedah-intermediate-13.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah hold that the Quran is the eternal, uncreated Speech (Kalam) of Allah, revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.

aqeedah-intermediate-14.question: What are the four levels of belief in Qadr according to classical scholars?
aqeedah-intermediate-14.explanation: Belief in Qadr includes: 1) Allah's eternal knowledge, 2) Writing in the Preserved Tablet, 3) Allah's Will, and 4) Allah's creation of all things.

aqeedah-intermediate-15.question: What is the Preserved Tablet called in Arabic?
aqeedah-intermediate-15.explanation: Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz is the Preserved Tablet where Allah has written the decree of all that will happen.

aqeedah-intermediate-16.question: What is the questioning in the grave conducted by?
aqeedah-intermediate-16.explanation: The two angels Munkar and Nakir question the deceased in the grave about their Lord, religion, and Prophet.

aqeedah-intermediate-17.question: What is the bridge that will be laid over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment?
aqeedah-intermediate-17.explanation: As-Siraat is the bridge over Jahannam that every person must cross; the righteous will pass safely while others may fall.

aqeedah-intermediate-18.question: What is Al-Mizan on the Day of Judgment?
options: The Pool of the Prophet ﷺ
aqeedah-intermediate-18.explanation: Al-Mizan is the Scale set up to weigh the good and bad deeds of people with perfect justice.

aqeedah-intermediate-19.question: What is Al-Hawd?
options: The Pool of the Prophet ﷺ from which believers will drink
aqeedah-intermediate-19.explanation: Al-Hawd is the Pool (Basin) granted to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ; those who drink from it will never feel thirst again.

aqeedah-intermediate-20.question: What is the belief regarding seeing Allah in the Hereafter according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: The believers will see Allah in Paradise
It is only a metaphorical vision
aqeedah-intermediate-20.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that the believers will see Allah with their eyes in the Hereafter as a great blessing, without encompassing Him.

aqeedah-intermediate-21.question: What is the status of the Companions (Sahabah) in the creed of Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: They are ordinary people with no special status
They are the best of generations and must be respected and loved
Only a few of them are reliable
They should be criticized for their differences
aqeedah-intermediate-21.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah love and honor all the Companions, recognizing them as the best generation after the Prophets.

aqeedah-intermediate-22.question: What is the correct belief about the intercession (Shafa'ah) of the Prophet ﷺ?
options: The Prophet ﷺ will intercede by Allah's permission on the Day of Judgment
aqeedah-intermediate-22.explanation: The greatest intercession belongs to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and all intercession occurs only by Allah's permission and pleasure.

aqeedah-intermediate-23.question: What is the term for the period between death and the Day of Resurrection?
aqeedah-intermediate-23.explanation: Al-Barzakh is the intermediate realm where souls remain after death until the Resurrection.

aqeedah-intermediate-24.question: Which of the following is an example of major shirk?
options: Calling upon a deceased saint for help
aqeedah-intermediate-24.explanation: Directing acts of worship such as dua (supplication) to anyone other than Allah constitutes major shirk.

aqeedah-intermediate-25.question: What does the Name of Allah 'Al-Quddus' mean?
options: The Holy, Free from all imperfection
aqeedah-intermediate-25.explanation: Al-Quddus means the Absolutely Pure and Holy One who is free from any deficiency or imperfection.

aqeedah-intermediate-26.question: What is the correct belief about human free will in relation to Qadr?
options: Humans have no free will at all
Humans have free will and are responsible for their choices, while Allah's decree encompasses all
Qadr means humans are forced in every action
aqeedah-intermediate-26.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm both divine decree and human responsibility; humans choose and act, and Allah creates their actions.

aqeedah-intermediate-27.question: What is the meaning of 'La ilaha illallah'?
options: There is no creator except Allah
There is no god truly worthy of worship except Allah
aqeedah-intermediate-27.explanation: The Kalima of Tawhid negates all false objects of worship and affirms that only Allah deserves worship.

aqeedah-intermediate-28.question: Which of the following is a condition for the acceptance of the Shahadah?
options: Simply uttering the words without understanding
Knowledge, certainty, sincerity, truthfulness, love, submission, and acceptance
Being born into a Muslim family only
aqeedah-intermediate-28.explanation: The Shahadah has conditions including knowledge of its meaning, certainty, sincerity (ikhlas), truthfulness, love, submission, and acceptance.

aqeedah-intermediate-29.question: What is the belief of Ahlus-Sunnah regarding the Attributes of Allah such as His Hand, Face, and Rising over the Throne?
options: They are affirmed as real without asking how (bila kayf) and without likening to creation
They mean Allah has a body like humans
aqeedah-intermediate-29.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm the Attributes as they came in the texts, without tashbih, ta'til, or asking 'how'.

aqeedah-intermediate-30.question: What is the Throne of Allah called in Arabic?
aqeedah-intermediate-30.explanation: Al-Arsh is the Throne of Allah, the greatest of His creations, over which He rose in a manner befitting His Majesty.

aqeedah-intermediate-31.question: What is Al-Kursi?
options: The Footstool of Allah, which extends over the heavens and earth
aqeedah-intermediate-31.explanation: Al-Kursi is the Footstool; its greatness is indicated in Ayat al-Kursi, and it is distinct from the Throne (Al-Arsh).

aqeedah-intermediate-32.question: What is the correct belief about the jinn?
options: They are a creation of Allah with free will, made from smokeless fire, and some are believers and some are not
They are the same as angels
aqeedah-intermediate-32.explanation: Jinn are real beings created from fire, possess free will, and will also be judged on the Day of Resurrection.

aqeedah-intermediate-33.question: What is the greatest sin in Islam?
aqeedah-intermediate-33.explanation: Shirk is the greatest sin because it violates the sole right of Allah to be worshipped, and Allah does not forgive it if one dies upon it without repentance.

aqeedah-intermediate-34.question: What is the term for the belief that faith increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience?
options: Iman is only in the heart
aqeedah-intermediate-34.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah hold that Iman consists of belief, speech, and action, and it increases with good deeds and decreases with sins.

aqeedah-intermediate-35.question: Who are the best of people after the Prophets according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ
aqeedah-intermediate-35.explanation: The Sahabah are the best generation; after them come the Tabi'in and then the Atba' at-Tabi'in.

aqeedah-intermediate-36.question: What is the correct belief about the return of Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him?
options: He will return near the end of time, kill the Dajjal, and rule with justice
He will return only as a spirit
aqeedah-intermediate-36.explanation: Authentic hadiths confirm that Prophet Isa (AS) will descend near the end of time, break the cross, kill the swine, and defeat the Dajjal.

aqeedah-advanced-1.question: What is the precise meaning of Tawhid al-Asma wa as-Sifat according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: Affirming Allah's Names and Attributes exactly as they appear in the texts, without tashbih, ta'til, takyif, or tahrif
Affirming Attributes while likening them to creation
aqeedah-advanced-1.explanation: The methodology of Ahlus-Sunnah is to affirm what Allah and His Messenger affirmed, negate what they negated, and remain silent where the texts are silent — without distortion, denial, asking how, or likening.

aqeedah-advanced-2.question: What is the difference between the Will of Allah (Al-Iradah) that is Kawniyyah and Shar'iyyah?
options: Kawniyyah is the universal creative will that always occurs; Shar'iyyah is the legislative will that Allah loves but may not occur if humans disobey
aqeedah-advanced-2.explanation: Allah's Kawni (universal) will encompasses everything that happens. His Shar'i (legislative) will is what He commands and loves; humans may choose to obey or disobey it.

aqeedah-advanced-3.question: What is the ruling on one who denies any of the six pillars of Iman?
options: He is a sinner but still a Muslim
He has left the fold of Islam (committed kufr)
He only needs to repent privately
It depends on the scholar's opinion only
aqeedah-advanced-3.explanation: Denial of any of the six pillars of Iman constitutes major disbelief (kufr akbar) that expels a person from Islam.

aqeedah-advanced-4.question: What is the correct understanding of Allah's Istiwa (rising) over the Throne?
options: It means Allah is sitting like a human
It is a real attribute of Allah in a manner befitting His Majesty, without asking how
It means Allah took control metaphorically
aqeedah-advanced-4.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm Allah's Istiwa over the Throne as mentioned in seven places in the Quran, without likening it to creation or denying it.

aqeedah-advanced-5.question: What is the meaning of Allah's Ma'iyyah (being with His creation)?
options: Allah is physically mixed with creation
Allah is with His creation by His knowledge, hearing, seeing, and power — a general and specific nearness
Allah is only in the heavens
Allah is everywhere in His Essence
aqeedah-advanced-5.explanation: Ma'iyyah is of two types: general (with all creation by knowledge and power) and specific (with the believers by support and protection). It does not mean mixing of essences.

aqeedah-advanced-6.question: What is the belief regarding the Speech of Allah (Kalamullah)?
options: It is an eternal Attribute of Allah; He speaks when He wills with letters and sound as befitting Him
It is only meanings without words
It is limited to the Quran only
aqeedah-advanced-6.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that Allah speaks with a real Speech that is uncreated; the Quran is part of His Speech revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.

aqeedah-advanced-7.question: What is the status of one who commits major sins according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: He is a Muslim with deficient Iman; under Allah's will — He may forgive or punish him
He is equal to the Prophets
aqeedah-advanced-7.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah do not declare the major sinner a kafir; he is a believer with weak faith and is subject to Allah's will in the Hereafter.

aqeedah-advanced-8.question: What is the correct position on the Companions who fought each other (e.g., the events of the Fitnah)?
options: We withhold from judging them, love them all, and believe they acted on ijtihad; the wrongdoer is forgiven
Only one side was completely right and the other is cursed
We must take sides and criticize openly
aqeedah-advanced-8.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah love all Sahabah, refrain from delving into their disputes, and hold that those who erred did so based on sincere ijtihad and are forgiven.

aqeedah-advanced-9.question: What is the belief about the Mahdi according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: A righteous man from the descendants of the Prophet ﷺ will appear near the end of time and fill the earth with justice
He is the same as Isa (AS)
aqeedah-advanced-9.explanation: Authentic hadiths establish the coming of the Mahdi, a leader from the family of the Prophet ﷺ who will rule with justice before the descent of Isa (AS).

aqeedah-advanced-10.question: What is the correct belief about the Dajjal (False Messiah)?
options: A real one-eyed man will appear as a major trial near the end of time and will be killed by Isa (AS)
He is the same as the Mahdi
aqeedah-advanced-10.explanation: The Dajjal is a real individual who will claim divinity, perform false miracles, and be a tremendous fitnah; Isa (AS) will kill him.

aqeedah-advanced-11.question: What is the ruling on seeking help (istighathah) from the dead?
options: It is major shirk because it directs an act of worship to other than Allah
It is permissible if the person was a saint
aqeedah-advanced-11.explanation: Calling upon the dead for help, relief, or intercession in matters only Allah can do is major shirk that nullifies Tawhid.

aqeedah-advanced-12.question: What is the difference between Tawassul that is permissible and that which is not?
options: Permissible Tawassul is through one's own good deeds, Allah's Names, or the living; forbidden is calling upon the dead or using them as intermediaries in worship
Only Tawassul through the Prophet ﷺ is allowed after his death by calling him
aqeedah-advanced-12.explanation: Permissible means of nearness include asking Allah by His Names, by one's righteous deeds, or requesting dua from a living righteous person. Calling upon the deceased is shirk.

aqeedah-advanced-13.question: What is the belief of Ahlus-Sunnah regarding the punishment and bliss in the grave?
options: It is real for both the body and soul; the believer experiences bliss and the disbeliever or major sinner experiences punishment
There is no experience in the grave
aqeedah-advanced-13.explanation: Authentic hadiths establish that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of Hellfire.

aqeedah-advanced-14.question: What is the correct understanding of Allah's Nuzul (descent) to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night?
options: It is metaphorical for His mercy
It is a real descent befitting His Majesty, without likening to creation
It means Allah leaves the Throne
aqeedah-advanced-14.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm the Nuzul as reported in the authentic hadiths, in a manner that befits Allah, without takyif or tashbih.

aqeedah-advanced-15.question: What is the status of the one who mocks or reviles Allah, His Messenger, or the religion?
options: He is a sinner but remains Muslim
He has committed major kufr and left Islam
He only needs to seek forgiveness
aqeedah-advanced-15.explanation: Reviling Allah, His Messenger, or Islam is major disbelief that expels a person from the religion, whether done seriously or in jest.

aqeedah-advanced-16.question: What is the belief about the creation of the actions of the servants?
options: Humans create their own actions independently
Allah creates the actions of the servants while they perform them by their will and choice
Actions are neither created nor real
Only good actions are created by Allah
aqeedah-advanced-16.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah hold that Allah is the Creator of everything, including the actions of humans, while humans are the doers who choose and are held accountable.

aqeedah-advanced-17.question: What is the correct position on the Names of Allah that are mentioned in the Quran and Sunnah?
options: We may invent new Names based on reason
We affirm only those Names established in the Quran and authentic Sunnah
All beautiful words can be used as Names
Names are limited to ninety-nine only
aqeedah-advanced-17.explanation: The Names of Allah are tawqifiyyah (based solely on revelation); we do not invent Names that are not reported in the texts.

aqeedah-advanced-18.question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'bila kayf' in the methodology of Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: Without asking 'how' and without likening to creation
aqeedah-advanced-18.explanation: Bila kayf means we affirm the Attribute as real while refraining from asking about its modality, because the 'how' is known only to Allah.

aqeedah-advanced-19.question: What is the ruling on denying the punishment of the grave?
options: It is a minor difference of opinion
It is a serious deviation; authentic hadiths establish it, and denying them is rejected
It is acceptable in modern times
aqeedah-advanced-19.explanation: The punishment and bliss of the grave are established by mutawatir (mass-transmitted) meaning in the Sunnah; denying them is a deviation from the creed of Ahlus-Sunnah.

aqeedah-advanced-20.question: What is the correct belief about the intercession of the angels, Prophets, and righteous?
options: There is no intercession at all
Intercession is real and occurs only by Allah's permission and for those with whom He is pleased
aqeedah-advanced-20.explanation: Allah grants permission for intercession to whom He wills; the greatest intercession is that of the Prophet ﷺ, followed by others among the angels, Prophets, and righteous.

aqeedah-advanced-21.question: What is the position of Ahlus-Sunnah on the issue of the Quran being created or uncreated?
options: The Quran is the uncreated Speech of Allah
The letters are created but the meaning is not
It is a matter of indifference
aqeedah-advanced-21.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah unanimously hold that the Quran is the eternal, uncreated Kalam of Allah. The view that it is created is a major innovation (bid'ah).

aqeedah-advanced-22.question: What is the correct understanding of the hadith 'Whoever dies while knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise'?
options: Simply uttering the words is enough regardless of action or belief
It means the one who dies upon pure Tawhid, free from major shirk, will eventually enter Paradise.
It means no deeds are required at all
It applies only to the Companions
aqeedah-advanced-22.explanation: The hadith affirms that the one who dies upon Tawhid will enter Paradise, though major sinners among them may first undergo purification in Hellfire if Allah wills.

aqeedah-advanced-23.question: What is the belief regarding the Ru'yah (seeing) of Allah in this world?
options: No one can see Allah in this world with their eyes; the believers will see Him only in the Hereafter
The Prophet ﷺ saw Allah with his eyes on earth
aqeedah-advanced-23.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah hold that Allah cannot be seen in this worldly life; the vision is a special blessing reserved for the believers in Paradise.

aqeedah-advanced-24.question: What is the correct creed regarding the parents of the Prophet ﷺ?
options: According to authentic reports, they died upon the religion of their people (pre-Islamic); the matter is left to Allah
aqeedah-advanced-24.explanation: Authentic hadiths indicate that the parents of the Prophet ﷺ died in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance; their ultimate fate is with Allah.

aqeedah-advanced-25.question: What is the ruling on one who claims that the companions of the Prophet ﷺ apostatized after his death (except a few)?
options: It is a valid historical opinion
It is a major deviation and a form of rejection of the Quran and Sunnah that praise the Companions
It is accepted by some schools
aqeedah-advanced-25.explanation: Claiming mass apostasy of the Sahabah contradicts clear Quranic praise and the consensus of Ahlus-Sunnah; it is a hallmark of certain deviant sects.

aqeedah-advanced-26.question: What is the correct belief about the miracles (mu'jizat) of the Prophets?
options: They are real acts that Allah caused to occur at the hands of His Prophets as proof of their truthfulness
They were performed by the Prophets independently
aqeedah-advanced-26.explanation: Miracles are extraordinary events that Allah allows His Prophets to display as evidence that they are truly sent by Him.

aqeedah-advanced-27.question: What is the belief of Ahlus-Sunnah concerning the Scale (Mizan) on the Day of Judgment?
options: It is only metaphorical for justice
It is a real Scale with two pans that will weigh the deeds of the servants
It is not mentioned in authentic texts
aqeedah-advanced-27.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm the reality of the Mizan as described in the Quran and authentic Sunnah; deeds will be weighed with perfect precision.

aqeedah-advanced-28.question: What is the correct understanding of the hadith about the seventy-three sects?
options: The saved sect is the one that follows the Quran, Sunnah, and the way of the Companions (Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah)
aqeedah-advanced-28.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ informed that the ummah would split into seventy-three sects; the saved one is that which is upon what he and his Companions were upon.

aqeedah-advanced-29.question: What is the position of Ahlus-Sunnah on the Attributes of Allah that are mentioned in the dual form (e.g., Hands)?
options: They are affirmed as real dual Attributes befitting Allah, without likening to creation
aqeedah-advanced-29.explanation: When the texts mention Allah's two Hands, Ahlus-Sunnah affirm them as real Attributes without tashbih or ta'til.

aqeedah-advanced-30.question: What is the correct creed regarding the Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj)?
options: It was a real, physical journey of the Prophet ﷺ by body and soul from Makkah to Jerusalem and then to the heavens
aqeedah-advanced-30.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that the Isra and Mi'raj occurred with the Prophet's body and soul while he was awake, as a great miracle.

aqeedah-advanced-31.question: What is the ruling on one who believes that the awliya (saints) have independent control over the universe?
options: It is a high level of faith
It is major shirk because control of the universe belongs only to Allah
aqeedah-advanced-31.explanation: Believing that any created being has independent power to control benefit, harm, or the universe is a form of major shirk in Rububiyyah.

aqeedah-advanced-32.question: What is the correct belief about the fate of the children of disbelievers who die before the age of puberty?
options: Their fate is left to the knowledge and justice of Allah; some reports indicate they are tested
aqeedah-advanced-32.explanation: The most cautious position of Ahlus-Sunnah is to entrust their affair to Allah; authentic reports mention a test for them on the Day of Judgment.

aqeedah-advanced-33.question: What is the meaning of the statement of Imam Malik when asked about Istiwa?
options: Istiwa is known, its 'how' is unknown, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is innovation
aqeedah-advanced-33.explanation: Imam Malik's famous reply encapsulates the methodology of the Salaf: affirm the Attribute, consign the modality to Allah, and avoid speculative questioning.

aqeedah-advanced-34.question: What is the correct position on the issue of whether Allah is above His creation?
options: Allah is everywhere in His Essence
Allah is above His creation, risen over the Throne, distinct from His creation
Direction does not apply to Allah at all
aqeedah-advanced-34.explanation: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above the heavens, risen over the Throne, separate from His creation, as indicated by numerous Quranic verses and hadiths.

aqeedah-advanced-35.question: What is the belief regarding the finality of Prophethood?
options: Prophets may still come after Muhammad ﷺ
Muhammad ﷺ is the final Prophet and Messenger; anyone claiming prophethood after him is a liar and kafir
Only Messengers have ended, not Prophets
The door of Prophethood is open for reformers
aqeedah-advanced-35.explanation: The Quran and authentic Sunnah establish that Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets; belief in any prophet after him is major disbelief.

aqeedah-advanced-36.question: What is the comprehensive definition of Iman according to Ahlus-Sunnah?
options: Belief in the heart, speech of the tongue, and actions of the limbs; it increases and decreases
aqeedah-advanced-36.explanation: Iman according to Ahlus-Sunnah is statement and action: belief of the heart, affirmation of the tongue, and deeds of the limbs, and it fluctuates with obedience and disobedience.
